sampling_model.design: Known independent Bernoulli assignment with probability \(1/2\); assignment is the only sampling randomness.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population on \(r\) disjoint copies of a fixed known motif \(H\) with minimum degree two.
sampling_model.treatment: Each \(Z_{ka}\) is independent, and exposure is \(T_{ka}(Z)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every motif assignment has positive probability \(2^{-h}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. Baselines and direct effects are fixed adversarial nuisances; converse priors mix deterministic schedules only as a proof device.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: ArXiv version 2 Section 4 and Appendix B construct the Bernoulli quadratic-weight statistic; Proposition 4.1 states its \(d_{\max}^5/n\) MSE envelope using the variance ingredients in Lemmas S3--S4.
Theorem 2 establishes asymptotic validity for an estimated-residual randomization test while leaving theoretical power open.
Section 5 gives the Riesz representer and unbiased estimator and notes possible gains from alternative weights.
Proposition 3 gives a design-based Le Cam lower bound for squared-error estimation.
Theorems 1 and 2 match quadratic tests and mixture lower bounds in random-design regression.
Proposition 1 and Section 5 obtain exact nonsharp-null tests through focal artificial experiments.
Theorems 1 and 2 give valid conditional tests when the focal statistic is imputable.
The paper gives conditional tests for hierarchical interference specifications.

body.tldr: Using the Bernoulli-half moment-reproduction identities and quadratic weight imported from GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 Section 4 and Appendix B, this project studies a fixed network motif repeated under Bernoulli assignment. A \(2^h\)-row assignment table yields an exact robust semialgebraic program for the attained worst-schedule assignment-conditional variance and its least-favourable-prior dual. For a LinkedIn-style Bernoulli network experiment with a known repeated local motif, the contact-set certificate selects among feasible exposure-quadratic weights by the smallest worst bounded-schedule conditional-variance constant. The same table gives the explicit affinity factor \(L_H\), with exact constants for \(K_3\) and \(C_4\). The optimal quadratic statistic is calibrated at finite-sample level over every bounded no-spillover schedule, and its fourth-root RMS signal scale is unavoidable for every measurable test. A maximality audit proves that Gao's weight is minimax for every minimum-degree-two motif of maximum degree at most three and is the unique minimizer on the complete five-vertex motif, so no strict weight improvement is claimed from these smallest non-degree-two cases. Whether another motif with maximum degree at least four yields a strict weight gain, and whether the quadratic test attains the exact local power constant, remain open.

project_justification.gap: GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 arXiv version 2 Section 4 and Appendix B supply the Bernoulli quadratic-weight construction, while Proposition 4.1 gives a \(d_{\max}^5/n\) MSE envelope from Lemmas S3--S4; available randomization tests provide validity without a theoretical local-power frontier.
project_justification.niche: Repeated fixed motifs isolate graph geometry from growing-degree asymptotics while preserving the practical Bernoulli design.
project_justification.fill: The project computes the attained variance saddle from a \(2^h\)-row robust semialgebraic program, derives exact worst-null calibration by finite assignment and sign-pattern enumeration, and proves a matching all-test fourth-root lower bound with an explicit motif-computable Hellinger constant and exact \(K_3\) and \(C_4\) values. The maximality audit additionally proves that the published Gao weight cannot be strictly improved within the quadratic class on any minimum-degree-two motif of maximum degree at most three and is uniquely minimax on the complete five-vertex motif; a strict witness on another motif of maximum degree at least four is not claimed.

body.related_work: The Bernoulli-half moment-reproduction identities and quadratic weight are imported as background from GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 arXiv version 2 Section 4 and Appendix B. Its Proposition 4.1 gives a \(d_{\max}^5/n\) MSE envelope using the variance ingredients in Lemmas S3--S4. This paper is an informed-by comparator: the new repeated-motif results identify attained worst-schedule conditional-variance constants for \(K_3\) and \(C_4\), provide exact composite-null calibration, and prove the same fourth-root scale necessary for all tests. The maximality audit shows that Gao's weight is already minimax throughout the degree-two/degree-three motif class and uniquely minimax for the complete five-vertex motif, so no strict gain is claimed from these smallest non-degree-two cases. TiwariBasu2026 establishes validity for a different residual test but leaves theoretical local-power analysis unresolved. HarshawSavjeWang2022 informs the finite-dimensional Riesz geometry. KandirosHarshawSavje2026 informs the design-based Le Cam reduction. CommingesDalalyan2013 informs fourth-root quadratic testing. AtheyEcklesImbens2018, BasseFellerToulis2019, and HoshinoYanagi2026 provide focal-conditioning benchmarks without being theorem-level targets. Ni2026 surveys the design--power tension. PougetAbadieEtAl2019 supplies the LinkedIn-style Bernoulli network deployment.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The explicit hard-prior calculation proves a constant-factor converse. The bound \(H^2(P_{0,a},P_{1,a})\le C_{\cos}r\xi_Ha^4\) does not identify the exact local likelihood experiment or establish quadratic sufficiency. The exact maximality audit rules out a strict weight improvement for every minimum-degree-two motif of maximum degree at most three and for the complete five-vertex motif. Other motifs having a vertex of degree at least four remain unresolved locations for a strict gain. The exact local power function and quadratic completeness also remain open.
body.honest_scope: The claims proved here are the existing exact \(K_3\) and \(C_4\) constants, a fixed-motif input and certificate-verification bound, and a maximality audit of the smallest non-degree-two cases. Convexity and complement symmetry prove that Gao's weight minimizes worst bounded-schedule conditional variance for every minimum-degree-two motif of maximum degree at most three; direct complete-five-vertex enumeration proves that it is uniquely minimax there with motif value 2560. The Bernoulli-half moment-reproduction identities, Gao et al.'s squared-separation convention, and their quadratic weight remain imported background from GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 Section 4 and Appendix B. No strict weight improvement is claimed. Exact elimination of the eight- and sixteen-row programs supplies the \(K_3\) and \(C_4\) values; the decimals are algebraic evaluations, not simulations. A strict witness on another motif of maximum degree at least four and the exact local power constant remain open.
